assessment: Post-swap bookkeeping pass (decklist 6047837e800e). The seven verification-gated promotions are applied and off the books: Viscera Seer, Sanguine Bond, Cruel Celebrant, Purphoros, Kalitas, Herald's Horn and Throne of the God-Pharaoh are maindeck, all four Bond/Conqueror/Exquisite/Vito pairings are checker-verified two-card infinites (stacks 001/004/005/006), Throne-under-Bloodletter is a verified 14-per-opponent end-step drain with an honest not-a-table-kill bound (stack 007), and Purphoros is a verified 10-per-opponent per two-mana Vampire (stack 008) — the floor stays 4 throughout, exactly as every sideboard-facts delta predicted. What remains on the 34-card bench is a true sideboard: the full-step remainder (Elenda, Indulgent Aristocrat) held behind crisp play-pattern conditions, a defensive recall package (Gifted Aetherborn, Vampire Nighthawk) whose condition is the thinned deathtouch web the swaps knowingly created, designed answers (Cemetery Gatekeeper, Callous Bloodmage), and depth, spares, and misfits. One bookkeeping note for the record: manual_prose (Vol. 006, pre-swap) still calls the Sanguine Bond lines 'strongly indicated rather than verified' and Akroma's Memorial 'the deck's lone seven-drop' — stacks 005/006 and the applied swaps supersede both claims, and the prose should be regenerated rather than read as current.

swaps.when: Play-pattern condition, restated crisply: adopt when the applied aristocrats core (Seer + Celebrant + Grave Pact) is generating multiple creature deaths per turn cycle in actual games — Elenda is the wrath-math payoff of a death engine that now exists in the 99 but has not yet proved its tempo at the pilot's pods
swaps.why: Elenda collects a counter from every creature death anywhere — your Seer sacrifices, your Grave Pact edicts, the table's combat — and dies into X lifelink Vampire tokens doubled through Anointed Procession/Mondrak, each token entry now also a verified 2-damage Purphoros trigger (stack 008); Mavren Fein makes one token per combat off nontoken attackers only, a trickle the promoted death web outpaces.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves

swaps.when: Play-pattern condition, restated crisply: adopt once games show Viscera Seer dying to removal before the Grave Pact/Celebrant web fires — outlet redundancy is the purchase — AND the pilot's pods are not punishing the loss of the last one-mana deathtouch blocker; with Aetherborn and Nighthawk already benched, this cut leaves Vampire of the Dire Moon and Nighthawk Scavenger as the only deathtouch bodies, so it is the swap most likely to be reversed by the aggro matchup
swaps.why: A second one-mana lifelink Vampire outlet whose activation pays tribe-wide +1/+1 counters that compound with Cordial Vampire's death triggers and Edgar's attack trigger across the token board; the sideboard-facts delta is 4→4 and the cost is named above rather than hidden.

citations.quote: consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)

opens_lines.why_plausible: Deterministic table-kill, verified: 26 Bond resolutions from a 2-life seed, retargeting each fresh trigger, chain crosses opponent deaths, win via 104.2a — both halves enchantments, the hardest of the four pairings to interact with at instant speed
Deterministic table-kill, verified: 13 Bond resolutions from a 3-life seed, closing the 2x2 of gain/loss pairings; exactly one creature half, so one instant-speed removal window per iteration

Verified with an honest bound: after the stack-003 seven-attacker shape, seven tapped creatures (untapped Bloodletter does not count itself) doubled to 14 lost per opponent — PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill, a 15-life opponent survives at exactly 1; present it as 14-per-opponent reach, never as lethal-by-default

Verified: one two-mana Vampire cast through the stack-002 eminence doubling makes four simultaneous token entries = four separate Purphoros triggers, plus a fifth when the spell's own body resolves — 5 x 2 = 10 damage to each opponent

The frame's first new candidate: Grave Pact forces each other player to sacrifice per your creature death, and Kalitas replaces opponents' dying nontoken creatures with exile plus a Zombie for you — plausibly every edict your free tokens buy also denies death triggers and recursion while minting sac fodder, but the replacement/sacrifice interaction has not been resolved on the record

The frame's second new candidate — aristocrats ignition: Celebrant's death trigger both drains each opponent 1 and gains you 1, so with any verified loop pair on the battlefield a single creature death (yours, mid-combat, or under a wrath) should ignite the table-kill; the loops themselves are verified, the ignition-from-a-death path (trigger ordering, which event seeds the loop) is not

long_term_defaults.why: The full-step remainder, held behind its swap condition above: in when the applied death engine demonstrably generates multiple deaths per turn cycle, out until then — a payoff without its engine is a 4-mana 1/1
The other full-step remainder: outlet redundancy behind Viscera Seer, conditioned on the aggro matchup tolerating the loss of the last one-mana deathtouch blocker — see the swap entry

Return case, earned: the applied swaps benched two of the deck's four deathtouch bodies, leaving Vampire of the Dire Moon and Nighthawk Scavenger; if creature-aggro pods start connecting through the thinned web, Aetherborn is the first recall — a BB 2/3 deathtouch lifelink wall that also attacks well under three lords

Return case, paired with Aetherborn: the same thinned-deathtouch condition at three mana with flying — but it returns second, because Nighthawk Scavenger already covers the evasive-deathtouch job in its power-crept form, which is why it was cut for Kalitas

Return case: a deliberate voltron/alpha-strike pivot — if the pilot rebuilds toward one-swing kills, Memorial's board-wide haste, trample, and protection from black and red is the one-card enabler; in the current go-wide drain list it was the 7-mana ceiling card in a curve with one spell above five, and Akroma's Will covers the alpha job at instant speed

Return case, same pivot: on an Edgar commander-damage line, Blade under Grave Pact grows the wearer per death anywhere for one mana — voltron equipment in a deck whose verified kills are loops and each-opponent drains stays benched until that identity changes
No earned return case: a 2/1 flyer that cannot block, with no other text — it lost its slot to a free instant-speed sac outlet and no condition this deck meets brings it back
No earned return case: attacker-only first strike Stromkirk Captain already grants, plus one-at-a-time counters Edgar's own attack trigger outclasses — the narrowest buff in the collection
Return case: only alongside a real Blood-token package (Gluttonous Guest, Wedding Security, Strefan-centric draws); in the current 99 her Blood output feeds only Strefan, who makes his own

Nearest to a slot of everything else on the bench: sacrificing one eminence token for BBB pays Edgar's generic cost and pulls the goldfish median t6.6 cast forward — but the remaining cuts (Swiftfoot Boots, Bontu's Monument, Vanquisher's Banner) each protect something the mandate keeps; first in when one opens
Best pure draw engine on the bench — end-step pay-{2}-draw behind a gain-life condition this deck meets most turns; first in if the pilot reports running out of gas, ahead of Silvertongue
A repeatable Sign in Blood behind a trivially-met gain-2 condition; second draw option behind Markov Purifier
Best fair two-drop on the bench — taxes or generates lifelink Vampire tokens — but the standing mandate ranks engine extenders above fair bodies and no two-drop slot has opened

Only ~40 of 97 maindeck entries are black cards, so the top-of-library trigger is blind-off more often than on; Viscera Seer's scry can rig it, but a coin-flip lord is not a clean pick under any mandate

A non-Vampire Human triggering neither eminence nor lords; the counters arrive too sporadically to build a flying payoff around
